YEAR BOOK OF THE YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATIONS OF NORTH AMERICA
May 1, 1908, to April 30, 1909
Internet Archive: ymcayearbookand00amergoog — NOT lending-restricted, djvu text 1,096,459 bytes

THE CATALOGUE SAYS 1907. THE TITLE PAGE SAYS OTHERWISE.
--------------------------------------------------------
Internet Archive metadata gives `year: 1907, date: 1907`. The title page, at scan line 1381,
reads in full:

    YEAR BOOK
    OF THE
    YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN
    ASSOCIATIONS
    OF NORTH AMERICA
    May I. 1908, to April 30, 1909
    NEW YORK
    YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION PRESS
    1909

with "Copyright, 1909" on the verso. THIS IS THE 1909 VOLUME, covering the association year that
ended 30 April 1909. The catalogue is out by two years, which is now the fourth wrong year this
project has caught in this series and its neighbours.

IT MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL HERE. 1909 IS THE FIRST YEAR OF THIS PROJECT'S 1909-1920 HOLE. Taken
on its catalogue year the volume is a duplicate of one already held and would have been skipped.

A note on why the earlier title-page sweep missed it. The sweep pattern was /FOR (THE )?YEARS?
1[89]dd/, which catches "For the Year 1899." and finds NOTHING in this volume: this one dates
itself by the association year, "May 1, 1908, to April 30, 1909", with no "for the year" at all.
A null from a pattern is a fact about the pattern.

II. WHAT IS NEW, CHECKED BY GREP BEFORE BEING WRITTEN DOWN
==========================================================
  M. G. BROOKS — occurs NOWHERE in this project, neither in the repo nor anywhere in the 954-file
    cache. He is Montreal's BOYS' WORK DIRECTOR in 1909 and entered Association work in 1905.
    (Two other Brookses are in the cache — Bob Brooks and Lynne Brooks of the Canadian Camping
    world in the 1970s and 80s. Neither is him.)

  FRED G. WHITE — new, an Assistant who entered Association work in 1909, i.e. new in post.

  HERBERT C. PATTERSON — the FIRST NAME of the "H. C. Paterson, Montreal, Westmount, Physical,
    entered 08" that the 1921 volume gave and this project recorded in f_4964. Note the spelling:
    this volume prints PATTERSON with two t's, the 1921 volume PATERSON with one. Note also that
    the project separately holds a PHILIP G. PATERSON as the camp's 1923 director; NOTHING here
    connects the two men and they are not to be joined on a surname.

  J. E. MERRITT'S YEAR OF ENTRY IS 1894 — the year the camp was founded. He was already known
    here as Physical Director in the 1906, 1907 and 1908 volumes, succeeding W. H. Ball; his
    entry date was not.

  W. G. BROWN at McGill University, entered 07; F. C. McGONIGLE, Railroad Secretary, entered 09;
    E. R. ERFFING/ERVING, Railroad Assistant.

  C. C. HOLLAND continues as Central Department Chairman, as in 1907 and 1908.


III. THE THING WORTH NOTICING: HOLLIDAY IS NO LONGER BOYS' WORK DIRECTOR
=======================================================================
This project holds f_4967, built from the 1906, 1907 and 1908 volumes: W. J. Holliday entered
YMCA work in 1906, was an Assistant that year, and was MONTREAL'S BOYS' WORK DIRECTOR in both
1907 and 1908 — and he is the man the association's own 1931 report calls Kanawana's FIRST CAMP
DIRECTOR.

In this volume he is listed as "Asst.", and the Boys' Work Director is M. G. Brooks.

BOTH LISTINGS IN THE VOLUME AGREE. The branch directory prints "Asst., W. J. Holliday" and
"Boys' Work Dir., M. G. Brooks"; the alphabetical index prints "Holliday, W. J., Montreal, Que.,
Asst., 06", where the 1907 and 1908 volumes printed "Holliday, W. J., Montreal, Que., Boys, 06".
So the change is carried in two independent places in the same book and is not one OCR slip.

WHAT THAT IS AND IS NOT. It is a change of title in the association's own annual roster between
the 1908 and 1909 volumes. It is NOT, on this evidence, a demotion, a dispute, a departure, or
anything else with a motive attached: a title can change for a reorganisation, a secondment, an
illness, or because a man moved to a job the roster names differently. The volume says what he
was called and nothing about why. What it does establish is that KANAWANA'S FIRST CAMP DIRECTOR
WAS NOT THE ASSOCIATION'S BOYS' WORK DIRECTOR IN 1909, which is a year the project previously had
nothing for at all, and that the man in that post was M. G. Brooks.

IV. AND MONTREAL STILL HAS NO EDUCATIONAL DIRECTOR
==================================================
The "Ed. Dir." line is printed with no name against it — as it was in 1900, after E. G. Randal
left for Taunton. The 1906 volume had J. S. Jamieson in the post and the 1907 and 1908 volumes
W. H. Henderson, so it was filled and is now empty again. The next Educational Director this
project has is F. H. Spinney, at the CAMP rather than the association, from about 1917.

V. "KANAWANA" IN THIS VOLUME
============================
Zero occurrences, as in every volume of this series read so far.

QUERIES RUN: 'Montr' across the whole text; 'YEAR BOOK|OFFICIAL ROSTER|ASSOCIATION PRESS|copyright'
across the front matter to find the title page; 'kanawana'; and repo-wide greps on "M. G. Brooks",
"Brooks", "C. C. Holland", "Fred G. White", "Herbert C. Patterson", "H. C. Patterson",
"H. C. Paterson", "J. E. Merritt" and "Maclaren" before any of them was called new.
